title: Endpoint convergence for the planar Schrodinger equation
main_claim: For every f in H^{1/3}(R^2), the Gaussian-regularized Schrodinger evolution has a limit for every 0<t<1 on one full-measure set of x, and that limit tends to f*(x) as t goes to 0. This is the Sobolev endpoint s=1/3 of Carleson's problem in the plane. It is proved through a local maximal estimate, int_{B(x0,1)} sup_{0<=t<1}|e^{itΔ}f| <= C||f||_{H^{1/3}}, which in turn comes from a loss-free weak-L^p short-time estimate (p>2) at frequency N with constant N^{1/3} (Theorem 8.1 / Proposition 9.1).
coverage: Read in full and checked: the introduction, Sec 2 (preliminaries), Sec 8 (dyadic distribution theorem) and Sec 9 (endpoint). In Sec 9 I re-derived step by step: the frequency rescaling in Prop 9.1 (S(t)f_N=(2π)^{-2}N·Ev(Nx,N^2t), threshold N^{1/3}, area factor N^2 cancels L^4); the time-separation kernel bound; the mass bound e<=Cm^{2-2/p}; the spatial bound e<=C r^{2/3} m, including the parabolic rescaling of G_N(J,Q) and the r^{-4/3+4/p}m^{2-2/p}<=r^{2/3}m step; the interpolation alpha=3/2-1/p; the heavy-path Cauchy-Schwarz; the convexity deficit and the argument that the parents are distinct; the frequency Cauchy-Schwarz; the representative and Gaussian-limit construction. All of these hold. In Sec 8 I checked: the parameter order (p_max, eta, C_g, C_a, C_d, u, kappa, p, sigma, B); the sparse-range Chebyshev condition sigma+4(p-2)/(3kappa)<c_s; the cap-gain scaling m r^{-3}(rL)^4(g r^{1/3+eta})^{-p}; the peeling and prefix logic; the dimensional consistency of the cubic-mass inequality lambda^6 M0^3 <~ m^3 h^10 d1 d2 E1 E2(E1+E2); and the final energy sum giving m L^{4/3} D^{-c_s}. In Sec 6 I checked the 1D flat estimate in full: the broad count via the frame theorem gives min{(b1b2)^{-2},(b1b2)^2 g^{-6}}; the narrow child scaling gives g'=(9/10)g u^{1/3} and the contraction factor u^{1-p0/3}. In Sec 4 I checked the broad-saving saturation algebra (x=0, n=4, y=-4/3) and its reduction to Prop 3.1. Not verified in depth: the information/entropy-profile contradiction argument in Sec 3 beyond Lemmas 3.2-3.5 (the use of He's projection theorem and the polynomial-partitioning step); the proof of the bilinear frame theorem in Sec 5 beyond its statement, initial reduction and telescoping identity; the plate geometry in Sec 7. Sanity checks against Knapp, focusing and Bourgain-type examples found no contradiction with the claimed weak-L^p (2<p<=3) estimate at N^{1/3}.
